entry.title: Elizabeth Holmes Documentary 'You Can See Everything' Explores Psychological Manipulation
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | readtheprofile.com | source | hacker news

The A24-distributed documentary *You Can See Everything*, directed by Lance Oppenheim and Nathan Fielder, follows Elizabeth Holmes in the weeks leading up to her prison sentence. Rather than a traditional true-crime retelling, the film utilizes specific cinematic techniques to manipulate the audience's emotional response and perception of Holmes in real time.

Through the strategic use of camera angles, editing, and narrative sequencing, the documentary demonstrates how easily viewers can be swayed by storytelling. The author argues that the film serves as a psychological study on how emotional impressions drive belief, forcing viewers to confront their own susceptibility to media framing.

entry.title: Creating 88x31 Animated Button Books with ImageMagick
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | k.sosnierz.me | discussion

The article provides a technical guide for creating animated 88x31 pixel GIF "buttons" that scroll through text using ImageMagick and POSIX command-line utilities. The workflow utilizes cat, tr, fold, and sed to format text into small, digestible segments, which are then converted into an animated sequence using the convert tool.

To ensure text remains legible at very low resolutions, the author recommends using specialized fonts such as TomThumb. The tutorial also includes a Python script for text centering and uses the text of Moby Dick as a practical example.

entry.title: Game Developer Podcast Discusses Misconceptions in Game Writing
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

The Game Developer Podcast features Bruno Dias, Aysha Farah, and Andrea Saravia Pérez discussing common misconceptions in game writing and narrative design. Key myths addressed include the idea that screenwriting is identical to game writing, the assumption that players do not want to read, and the belief that stories are written before development begins.

The participants share professional insights from work on titles such as *Fallen London*, *Life is Strange: Double Exposure*, and *Sid Meier's Civilization VII*. The discussion highlights how these misconceptions can harm the development process and clarifies the role of narrative design within a production pipeline.

entry.title: decomp.dev Disables Main Index and New Project Tracking
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | decomp.dev | discussion | hacker news

decomp.dev, a platform launched in 2024 to track matching decompilation progress, is disabling its main index and the ability to add new projects. While the site will continue to host historical data and individual project pages, it will no longer serve as a centralized aggregator or public leaderboard for active efforts.

The decision stems from the impact of advanced AI models on the decompilation community. The site's creator, @encounter, cites the rise of low-effort, hostile forks of existing projects and the "racing" of unrefined ports by actors utilizing AI as primary drivers. These trends have reportedly led to a conflation of research-focused decompilation with superficial game porting, which the developer argues undermines the community's focus on understanding original source code.

entry.title: Mythfall Implements Procedural Mumble Speech for NPCs
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | youtube.com | discussion

The developer of Mythfall, a browser-based bullet hell MMO, has implemented a procedural "mumble speech" system for non-player characters. Instead of using recorded audio files, the system generates real-time vocalizations based on text input by mathematically modeling vocal folds, mouth resonance, and airflow. This creates human-like, non-verbal speech that adjusts dynamically to the text being displayed.

This approach reduces download sizes and allows for seamless dialogue updates during development. The system utilizes existing text punctuation to dictate speech rhythm and intonation, using question marks for rising pitch and commas for pauses. By adjusting pitch and resonance parameters, the developer can create distinct character identities, such as children or elderly NPCs, within a minimal memory footprint.

entry.title: Epic Games Rebuilds Easy Anti-Cheat for Linux
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | onlineservices.epicgames.com | discussion | hacker news

The new "EAC Linux v2" implementation seeks to provide a level of anti-cheat protection on Linux comparable to the Windows version. This overhaul aims to enable multiplayer games like Fortnite to run on Linux by leveraging existing system security features—including TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, and eBPF—rather than relying on a dedicated kernel module.

A pilot program in Fortnite will precede the release of the technology to other game developers. To facilitate this, Epic Games is working with Linux distribution maintainers to integrate well-known signing keys into the secure boot process and is requiring specific hardware configurations such as IOMMU and Kernel Lockdown Integrity Mode.

entry.title: Shield Battery Implements Rollback Netcode for StarCraft: Brood War
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | youtube.com | discussion

Shield Battery has implemented rollback netcode for StarCraft: Brood War, replacing the traditional lockstep networking model. This system allows player commands to execute on the very next frame, significantly reducing the input latency experienced during online matches.

The netcode predicts player actions and only corrects the game state when unexpected commands arrive, transforming lag spikes into minor visual "hops" rather than total freezes. Additionally, latency adjustments are applied to each player's connection individually, ensuring that a single player's poor connection does not delay the entire match.

entry.title: Owlchemy CEO: VR Remains an Emerging Market Due to Hardware Form Factor
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com

Andrew Eiche, CEO of Owlchemy Labs, argues that the virtual reality market has not yet achieved mainstream status because current hardware lacks the streamlined form factor required for public use. He compares current headsets to the Nintendo Entertainment System, suggesting the technology must undergo further "societal iteration" before it is no longer viewed as a novelty.

Addressing recent industry layoffs, Eiche suggests that some studios have failed to align with player data, specifically overlooking the popularity of social games with high embodiment. By contrast, Owlchemy reports record engagement metrics for Dimensional Double Shift by focusing on these proven user preferences.
